## Proof

**Setup.** Let $V$ be a 4-dimensional real vector space with a nondegenerate symmetric bilinear form $Q$ of signature $(3,1)$, and let $e_0 \in V$ be a timelike unit vector ($Q(e_0)<0$). Its orthogonal complement $W := e_0^\perp$ is a 3-dimensional positive-definite subspace. The inclusion
$$i: SO(W) \cong SO(3) \hookrightarrow SO^+(V) \cong SO^+(3,1), \qquad R \mapsto (e_0 \mapsto e_0,\; w \mapsto Rw),$$
identifies $SO(3)$ with the subgroup of $SO^+(3,1)$ fixing $e_0$. We show this lifts to an injection $\iota: Spin(3) \hookrightarrow Spin(3,1)$ with $\pi_{3,1}\circ\iota = i\circ\pi_3$.

---

**Construction via the Clifford algebra.** Let $Cl(V,Q)$ be the Clifford algebra. Since $V = W \oplus \mathbb{R}e_0$ is an orthogonal direct sum of nondegenerate subspaces, there is a natural injective algebra homomorphism
$$j: Cl(W, Q|_W) \hookrightarrow Cl(V,Q), \qquad w \mapsto w \quad(\text{viewed as a vector of } V),$$
which is well defined because the defining relation $w^2 = Q|_W(w) = Q_V(w)$ is preserved. Being an even-degree-preserving map (vectors map to vectors), $j$ restricts to an injective algebra homomorphism on the even subalgebras:
$$j: Cl^0(W) \hookrightarrow Cl^0(V).$$

Recall
$$Spin(3) = \big\{ w_1\cdots w_{2k} \in Cl^0(W) : w_i \in W,\; Q(w_i)=1 \big\},$$
$$Spin(3,1) = \big\{ v_1\cdots v_{2k} \in Cl^0(V) : v_i \in V,\; Q(v_i)=\pm 1,\; \widetilde{\mathrm{Ad}}_g(V)\subseteq V \big\},$$
where $\widetilde{\mathrm{Ad}}_g(x) = \alpha(g)\,x\,g^{-1}$ and $\alpha$ is the grade involution. Every unit spacelike vector $w_i \in W$ is a unit vector of $V$ (with $Q_V(w_i)=+1$), so $j$ sends products of an even number of unit vectors of $W$ to products of an even number of unit vectors of $V$. Hence $j$ restricts to a group homomorphism
$$\iota := j|_{Spin(3)}: Spin(3) \longrightarrow Spin(3,1).$$
Since $j$ is an injective algebra homomorphism, $\iota$ is **injective**.

---

**Commutativity with the covering maps.** The covering map $\pi_{3,1}: Spin(3,1) \to SO^+(3,1)$ is the twisted adjoint action $\pi_{3,1}(g)(x) = \alpha(g)\,x\,g^{-1}$, and likewise $\pi_3(g)(w) = \alpha(g)\,w\,g^{-1}$ for $g\in Spin(3)\subset Cl^0(W)$. We must show that for every $g\in Spin(3)$,
$$\pi_{3,1}(\iota(g)) = i(\pi_3(g)) \quad\text{as elements of } SO^+(3,1).$$

Both sides are linear isometries of $V$; we check them on the splitting $V = \mathbb{R}e_0 \oplus W$.

*On $W$:* For $w\in W$, since $\iota(g)=g$ as an element of $Cl^0(V)$ and $\alpha(g)=g$ (because $g$ is even),
$$\pi_{3,1}(\iota(g))(w) = g\,w\,g^{-1} = \pi_3(g)(w) = i(\pi_3(g))(w).$$

*On $e_0$:* Write $g = w_1\cdots w_{2k}$ with $w_i \in W$. Each $w_i$ is orthogonal to $e_0$, so $w_i e_0 = -e_0 w_i$ in $Cl(V)$. Hence
$$g\,e_0 = w_1\cdots w_{2k}\,e_0 = (-1)^{2k} e_0\, w_1\cdots w_{2k} = e_0\, g,$$
i.e. $g$ commutes with $e_0$. Therefore
$$\pi_{3,1}(\iota(g))(e_0) = g\,e_0\,g^{-1} = e_0 = i(\pi_3(g))(e_0).$$

The two maps agree on both summands, so $\pi_{3,1}\circ\iota = i\circ\pi_3$.

---

**Conclusion.** The natural Clifford-algebra inclusion $Cl^0(W)\hookrightarrow Cl^0(V)$ restricts to an injective group homomorphism $\iota: Spin(3)\to Spin(3,1)$, and the computation above shows the diagram

$$\begin{array}{ccc} Spin(3) & \xrightarrow{\;\iota\;} & Spin(3,1) \\[2pt] \downarrow{\pi_3} & & \downarrow{\pi_{3,1}} \\[2pt] SO(3) & \xrightarrow{\;i\;} & SO^+(3,1) \end{array}$$

commutes. Hence **yes**, the inclusion $SO(3)\hookrightarrow SO^+(3,1)$ induces an injection $Spin(3)\hookrightarrow Spin(3,1)$ commuting with the covering maps.

## Proof

**Setup.** Let $V$ be a 4-dimensional real vector space with a nondegenerate symmetric bilinear form $Q$ of signature $(3,1)$, and let $e_0 \in V$ be a timelike unit vector ($Q(e_0)<0$). Its orthogonal complement $W := e_0^\perp$ is a 3-dimensional positive-definite subspace. The inclusion
$$i: SO(W) \cong SO(3) \hookrightarrow SO^+(V) \cong SO^+(3,1), \qquad R \mapsto (e_0 \mapsto e_0,\; w \mapsto Rw),$$
identifies $SO(3)$ with the subgroup of $SO^+(3,1)$ fixing $e_0$. We show this lifts to an injection $\iota: Spin(3) \hookrightarrow Spin(3,1)$ with $\pi_{3,1}\circ\iota = i\circ\pi_3$.

---

**Construction via the Clifford algebra.** Let $Cl(V,Q)$ be the Clifford algebra. Since $V = W \oplus \mathbb{R}e_0$ is an orthogonal direct sum of nondegenerate subspaces, there is a natural injective algebra homomorphism
$$j: Cl(W, Q|_W) \hookrightarrow Cl(V,Q), \qquad w \mapsto w \quad(\text{viewed as a vector of } V),$$
which is well defined because the defining relation $w^2 = Q|_W(w) = Q_V(w)$ is preserved. Being an even-degree-preserving map (vectors map to vectors), $j$ restricts to an injective algebra homomorphism on the even subalgebras:
$$j: Cl^0(W) \hookrightarrow Cl^0(V).$$

Recall
$$Spin(3) = \big\{ w_1\cdots w_{2k} \in Cl^0(W) : w_i \in W,\; Q(w_i)=1 \big\},$$
$$Spin(3,1) = \big\{ v_1\cdots v_{2k} \in Cl^0(V) : v_i \in V,\; Q(v_i)=\pm 1,\; \widetilde{\mathrm{Ad}}_g(V)\subseteq V \big\},$$
where $\widetilde{\mathrm{Ad}}_g(x) = \alpha(g)\,x\,g^{-1}$ and $\alpha$ is the grade involution. Every unit spacelike vector $w_i \in W$ is a unit vector of $V$ (with $Q_V(w_i)=+1$), so $j$ sends products of an even number of unit vectors of $W$ to products of an even number of unit vectors of $V$. Hence $j$ restricts to a group homomorphism
$$\iota := j|_{Spin(3)}: Spin(3) \longrightarrow Spin(3,1).$$
Since $j$ is an injective algebra homomorphism, $\iota$ is **injective**.

---

**Commutativity with the covering maps.** The covering map $\pi_{3,1}: Spin(3,1) \to SO^+(3,1)$ is the twisted adjoint action $\pi_{3,1}(g)(x) = \alpha(g)\,x\,g^{-1}$, and likewise $\pi_3(g)(w) = \alpha(g)\,w\,g^{-1}$ for $g\in Spin(3)\subset Cl^0(W)$. We must show that for every $g\in Spin(3)$,
$$\pi_{3,1}(\iota(g)) = i(\pi_3(g)) \quad\text{as elements of } SO^+(3,1).$$

Both sides are linear isometries of $V$; we check them on the splitting $V = \mathbb{R}e_0 \oplus W$.

*On $W$:* For $w\in W$, since $\iota(g)=g$ as an element of $Cl^0(V)$ and $\alpha(g)=g$ (because $g$ is even),
$$\pi_{3,1}(\iota(g))(w) = g\,w\,g^{-1} = \pi_3(g)(w) = i(\pi_3(g))(w).$$

*On $e_0$:* Write $g = w_1\cdots w_{2k}$ with $w_i \in W$. Each $w_i$ is orthogonal to $e_0$, so $w_i e_0 = -e_0 w_i$ in $Cl(V)$. Hence
$$g\,e_0 = w_1\cdots w_{2k}\,e_0 = (-1)^{2k} e_0\, w_1\cdots w_{2k} = e_0\, g,$$
i.e. $g$ commutes with $e_0$. Therefore
$$\pi_{3,1}(\iota(g))(e_0) = g\,e_0\,g^{-1} = e_0 = i(\pi_3(g))(e_0).$$

The two maps agree on both summands, so $\pi_{3,1}\circ\iota = i\circ\pi_3$.

---

**Conclusion.** The natural Clifford-algebra inclusion $Cl^0(W)\hookrightarrow Cl^0(V)$ restricts to an injective group homomorphism $\iota: Spin(3)\to Spin(3,1)$, and the computation above shows the diagram

$$\begin{array}{ccc} Spin(3) & \xrightarrow{\;\iota\;} & Spin(3,1) \\[2pt] \downarrow{\pi_3} & & \downarrow{\pi_{3,1}} \\[2pt] SO(3) & \xrightarrow{\;i\;} & SO^+(3,1) \end{array}$$

commutes. Hence **yes**, the inclusion $SO(3)\hookrightarrow SO^+(3,1)$ induces an injection $Spin(3)\hookrightarrow Spin(3,1)$ commuting with the covering maps.
